items.name: ci-plan
items.title: CI that tests a change by what it could break
items.description: A script that decides which slow CI jobs a run needs from the files a pull request changes, with its own test cases, and the workflow that reads it: a push to main repeats nothing its pull request passed on the same commit, a release's pull request gets one real update, and every night everything runs. For a repository on GitHub Actions; its files go to the repo root

items.name: upgrade-test
items.title: Upgrade test through the updater
items.description: Updates end to end against real Docker: every published release that can still update in one step is started with data in it and updated by the updater to the image under test, then a newer version, then one that dies after migrating and must be rolled back with its data. A hooks file holds what only the product knows. For an app that runs from a compose file with the updater; its files go to the repo root

items.name: release
items.title: Releases the updater can install
items.description: The release workflow of a self-hosted product: release-please keeps a release pull request and its checks are started for it; merging it builds, scans, smoke-tests, pushes and signs the image, publishes a signed release.json naming the image by digest and the compose file by hash, runs the updater's own signature checks against it, and opens the notes with docs/releases/<version>.md when there is one. For a repository with a Dockerfile and deploy/compose; its files go to the repo root
